info.name: Relavoi API v1.0.0
info.description:
Generated from openapi.yaml by scripts/openapi-to-postman.py. Do not edit by hand.

Import the environment file beside this one, call Authentication > "Exchange an API key and secret for an SDK token", and paste the accessToken into the environment's accessToken variable. Every other request sends it as a bearer token.

Relavoi connects two people by phone without either seeing the other's
number. You create a session for a pair of Nigerian mobile numbers, we
allocate a proxy number, and each party dials that proxy instead.

## Authentication

Every endpoint except `/health` and `/auth/*` takes a bearer JWT.

There are two kinds, and they are not interchangeable:

- An **SDK token**, from `POST /auth/token` with your API key and secret.
  This is what a mobile app or your backend uses to create sessions.
- A **dashboard token**, from `POST /auth/dashboard/login`. Some endpoints
  are dashboard-only, and some are restricted further by the user's role.

Tokens last 15 minutes. Mint a new one rather than trying to refresh.

## Conventions

- Timestamps are ISO 8601 with a `Z` offset.
- Phone numbers are Nigerian mobile numbers. `+2348012345678`,
  `08012345678` and `8012345678` are all accepted and normalised to E.164.
  Anything else is refused with `422 number-not-supported`.
- Money is an object: integer `kobo`, a formatted `display`, and `naira`.
- Lists are cursor-paginated. Pass `pagination.after` back as `after`.
- Errors are RFC 7807 `application/problem+json`.

item.name: Health
item.description: Liveness, and the state of the carrier circuit breaker.

request.description: No auth. Reports whether Postgres and Redis are reachable, and the commit the running image was built from.

`CLOSED` is normal. `OPEN` means the carrier is failing and new session
creation is refused; there is one provider, so nothing is rerouted.

item.name: Authentication
item.description: Exchanging credentials for a token, and managing API keys.

item.name: Exchange an API key and secret for an SDK token

request.description:
The one endpoint your backend calls with the secret. The key prefix
decides the mode: `rk_live_` gives a live token, `rk_test_` a sandbox
one. Rate limited per address.

item.name: Mint a short-lived token for one user's device

request.description:
Call this from your own backend, with a token from `/auth/token`. It
returns a token for one user, carrying only the scopes you ask for, and
it is what you hand your mobile app.

**Why this exists.** Every SDK's `initialize()` also accepts your API
key and secret, and anything compiled into a published app can be read
back out of it. A leaked live pair can create sessions billed to you
and list every session and call on your workspace. A device token can
do neither.

## Scopes

| Scope | Reaches |
|---|---|
| `sessions:verify` | `GET` and `POST /sessions/verify` |
| `sessions:read` | `GET /sessions/{id}`, and only sessions this user is a party to |
| `devices:write` | `POST` and `DELETE /devices/token`, `POST /devices/presence` |

Everything else refuses a device token with `403 scope-not-permitted`,
including creating, ending or retargeting a session, listing the
workspace's sessions or calls, and anything under `/config`,
`/billing`, `/webhooks`, `/numbers` or `/auth/keys`. A device token
also cannot mint another.

The WebSocket stream refuses device tokens: it fans out a whole
workspace's events, and narrowing it to one user is not built, so there
is no scope for it to grant.

## Lifetime

Fifteen minutes, and a floor of one minute. `ttlSeconds` outside that
is clamped rather than refused. Device tokens answer to the same
revocation as any other: suspending the workspace or rotating its API
key stops them on the next request.
Self-service signup. Returns a dashboard token for the new owner. No API credentials are minted; ask for them from the dashboard.
For a human in the console, not for an app. Rate limited to 10 attempts per 15 minutes per address.
Dashboard token, OWNER or ADMIN.

item.name: Sessions
item.description: The core object. A masked connection between two numbers.

request.description: List sessions

Allocates a proxy number for this pair and returns it. Both numbers must
be Nigerian mobile numbers in the same country.

The allocator guarantees no participant overlap: a number is never
serving two live sessions that share a party, which is what stops a
callback reaching the wrong person.
Fetch one session

item.name: Update metadata or the grace period

request.description: Update metadata or the grace period

Moves it to `GRACE_PERIOD`, so a follow-up call still connects. Send
`gracePeriodMinutes: 0` to cut contact off immediately.

item.name: Point the session at a different customer

request.description:
Keeps the proxy number and swaps party B, for a reassigned order. The
previous customer stops reaching anyone on that number.
Calls on one session
List calls
Fetch one call
Pool status by region

Dashboard token, OWNER. Provisioning is a manual process today, so this
answers `501` and records the request: it is logged against your
workspace and raises an alert with us, so asking here is how you ask.
Which carrier your numbers come from is ours to choose.

item.name: Webhooks
item.description: Where we send events, and what we got back.

request.description: Your webhook destination

The URL must be public: a private, loopback or link-local address is
refused, and so is a redirect that lands on one. Deliveries are signed
with `X-Relavoi-Signature`, an HMAC of `timestamp.body`.
Delivers a synthetic `session.created` to your registered URL, signed the same way a real one is, and reports what came back.

Every attempt, with the status code your endpoint returned. The response
body and the error text are not included: they are operator-only.
